problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.8 & 0.15 \\ 0.2 & 0.85\end{aligned}],\,q=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{7} \\ \frac{4}{7}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the stochastic matrix $P$ and vector $q$ shown above. Which of the following statements are true?

- $q$ is a stochastic vector
- $Pq=q$
- $q$ is a steady-state vector of $P$

choices.value: None of the statements are true

feedback.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.25 & 0.3 & 0.5 \\ 0.15 & 0.3 & 0.2 \\ 0.6 & 0.4 & 0.3\end{aligned}],\,q=[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{9} \\ \frac{4}{9} \\ \frac{1}{9}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the stochastic matrix $P$ and vector $q$ shown above. Which of the following statements are true?

- $q$ is a stochastic vector
- $Pq=q$
- $q$ is a steady-state vector of $P$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that a steady-state vector of a stochastic matrix $P$ is a stochastic vector $q$ such that $Pq=q.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, $q$ is a stochastic vector since its entries are non-negative and add up to $1.$

- Statement II is false. Note that

$$
Pq=[\begin{aligned}0.25 & 0.3 & 0.5 \\ 0.15 & 0.3 & 0.2 \\ 0.6 & 0.4 & 0.3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{9} \\ \frac{4}{9} \\ \frac{1}{9}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1.2}{9}+\frac{0.5}{9} \\ \frac{0.6}{9}+\frac{1.2}{9}+\frac{0.2}{9} \\ \frac{2.4}{9}+\frac{1.6}{9}+\frac{0.3}{9}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2.7}{9} \\ \frac{2}{9} \\ \frac{4.3}{9}\end{aligned}]\ne q.
$$

- Statement III is false. Since $Pq\ne q,$ it is not a steady-state vector of $P.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
